title: Tests for Vision and Normal Optics of Eyes

questions.q: Minimum resolvable component of visual acuity per p117:
opts: Tested clinically; MAR = 2 points subtending an angle
Cannot be measured by clinical tests
questions.exp: Minimum resolvable: tested clinically; MAR (minimum angle of resolution) = 2 points subtending an angle. (Book p117)

questions.q: Per p117, two points subtending an angle of <30-60 seconds on the eye:
questions.exp: <30-60 seconds: on eye can't be viewed separately; >30-60 seconds: can be viewed separately. (Book p117)

questions.q: All relate to minimum discriminable/hyperacuity per p117 EXCEPT:
opts: Cannot be measured by clinical tests
questions.exp: Hyperacuity: cannot be measured by clinical tests; eg stereopsis (3D vision), vernier acuity. MAR belongs to minimum resolvable. (Book p117)

questions.q: Snellen fraction 6/24 per p117: numerator 6 = ___; denominator 24 = ___.
opts: Total number of letters seen; number of rows attempted
Distance in metres; equivalent distance in feet
Minutes of arc subtended; seconds of arc subtended
Distance of examination (in m); respective minimum distance at which normal eye can visualize the row
questions.exp: 6 → distance of examination (in m); 24 → respective distance: minimum distance at which normal eye can visualize the row. (Book p117)

questions.q: Snellen's chart structure per p117:
opts: Minimum 7 rows of letters; variable letters per row; each eye tested separately
questions.exp: Minimum 7 rows of letters; number of letters per row variable; each eye tested separately. (Book p117)

questions.q: A patient cannot read 6/60 at 6 m per p117 flowchart. Next step:
opts: Move patient closer in increments of 1 m until a larger row is visible
questions.exp: If even 6/60 not visible at 6 m → move patient closer in increments of 1 m until larger row is visible → record acuity (eg 3/60 if largest row seen at 3 m). (Book p117)

questions.q: Per p117, if the largest row is seen at 3 m the recorded acuity is ___; if nothing visible until 1 m, next test is ___.
questions.exp: 3/60 if largest row seen at 3 m; if not visible until 1 m → finger counting close to face → FCCF+; if negative → hand movements HM(+); if not perceived → light PL+; if negative → patient blind. (Book p117)

questions.q: Worst-to-best sequence of poor-vision recording per p117:
questions.exp: Rows → finger counting (FCCF+) → hand movements (HM+) → light perception (PL+) → patient blind. (Book p117)

questions.q: Least acuity discernible via Snellen's chart per p118:
questions.exp: Note: least acuity discernible via Snellen's chart: 1/60. (Book p118)

questions.q: Principle per p118: each optotype subtends ___ at the nodal point when viewed from its respective distance; each segment subtends 1 minute.
questions.exp: Each optotype subtends angle of 5 minutes of arc at nodal point of eye; angle subtended by each segment = 1' (> MAR); total angle = 5'. (Book p118)

questions.q: Angle (in minutes) subtended at variable distance X per p118 equals:
questions.exp: Angle (in minutes) = respective distance / given distance (X) × 5'. (Book p118)

questions.q: Match per p118 — 1) Landolt C ring chart 2) Snellen's E chart 3) Bailey-Lovie/logMAR chart … A) Direction identification test with broken rings B) Direction identification test with letter E C) Constant 5 letters per row, log value, not used in India
questions.exp: Direction identification tests used in illiterate patients: Landolt C ring chart, Snellen's E chart; Bailey-Lovie/logMAR: constant 5 letters per row, log value, not used in India. (Book p118)

questions.q: Which statement on Bailey-Lovie/logMAR chart per p118 is TRUE?
opts: 5 letters/row; log acuity; no crowding; not used in India
Widely used across India for recording log acuity
Shows marked crowding phenomenon at lower visual acuity
Variable letters per row exactly like Snellen's chart but tested at 3 m
questions.exp: Number of letters per row constant (5); log value used to record acuity; not used in India; advantages: no crowding phenomenon, increased accuracy at lower visual acuity. (Book p118)

questions.q: Direction identification tests per p118 are used for:
questions.exp: Direction identification tests used in illiterate patients: Landolt C ring chart and Snellen's E chart. (Book p118)

questions.q: Match verbal tests for school children (2-5 yrs) per p119 — 1) Sheridan Gardiner 2) STYCAR 3) Key picture / Broken wheel / Allen cards … A) Letter matching: HOTV test, child matches letters on cards/tiles B) Screening in young children and the intellectually disabled C) Picture matching tests
questions.exp: Matching of letters: Sheridan Gardiner HOTV test (child matches letters on cards/tiles), STYCAR (screening in young children and the intellectually disabled); matching of pictures: key picture test, broken wheel test, Allen picture card preschool test. (Book p119)

questions.q: Sheridan Gardiner test per p119:
opts: HOTV test — child matches letters on the cards/tiles
questions.exp: Sheridan Gardiner: HOTV test; child matches letters on the cards/tiles. (Book p119)

questions.q: OKN drum per p119 tests ___ acuity; thinner the strip perceived → higher the acuity.
questions.exp: OKN drum: variable thickness of strip; thinner the strip perceived → higher the acuity; resolvable acuity (MAR) tested. (Book p119)

questions.q: Carford drum per p119 uses dots of varying sizes; smaller the dots visualized → higher acuity; it tests ___ acuity.
questions.exp: Carford drum: dots of varying sizes; smaller the dots visualized → higher acuity; detection acuity tested. (Book p119)

questions.q: Preferential looking test (PLT) per p119:
opts: Infant prefers plain over striped areas during the test
The stripes progressively widen as the infant's acuity improves
Prefers stripes; narrowing stripes; thinner seen → ↑ acuity
Uses vanishing optotype cards instead of stripes
questions.exp: An infant prefers to look at striped over plain areas; progressive narrowing of stripes; thinner the stripes visualized → ↑ acuity. Types: Teller acuity cards, Keeler gratings. (Book p119)

questions.q: Cardiff Acuity Test (CAT) per p119:
opts: Used in both infants and toddlers; based on vanishing optotype
questions.exp: Cardiff Acuity Test: used in both infants and toddlers; based on vanishing optotype. (Book p119)

questions.q: VEP principle per p119:
opts: Light stimulus → visual pathway → ↑ visual cortex activity → normal VEP
questions.exp: Principle: light stimulus → visual pathway → ↑ visual cortex activity → normal VEP. (Book p119)

questions.q: Tests listed for infants per p119 include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Infant tests: OKN, PLT, CAT, VEP (+ indirect assessment). Sheridan Gardiner belongs to verbal tests for school children 2-5 yrs. (Book p119)

questions.q: Match indirect assessment reflexes per p120 — 1) Blink reflex 2) Menace reflex 3) VEP … A) Stimulus: approach of object near eye; response: closure of eyes; develops around 5 months B) Stimulus: illumination of eyes; response: blinking; present since birth C) Objective cortical response to light stimulus
questions.exp: Blink reflex present since birth; menace reflex develops around 5 months of age; VEP is objective. (Book p120)

questions.q: Menace reflex develops around ___ per p120.
questions.exp: Menace reflex develops around 5 months of age; blink reflex present since birth. (Book p120)

questions.q: Near vision tests per p120: main use and distance of examination:
opts: Diagnosis of presbyopia; 30-35 cm (comfortable reading distance)
questions.exp: Use: for diagnosis of presbyopia; distance of examination 30-35 cm (comfortable reading distance). (Book p120)

questions.q: Snellen's near chart grades per p120: best = ___, worst = ___.
questions.exp: Snellen's near chart (m/c): N6 (best), N8, N12, N24, N36 (worst). (Book p120)

questions.q: Jaeger's chart results per p120 range between:
questions.exp: Jaeger's chart: results between J1 → J7; also Roman test type. (Book p120)

questions.q: Least distance of distinct vision (near point) per p120:
questions.exp: Note: least distance of distinct vision (near point) = 25 cm. (Book p120)

questions.q: Contrast sensitivity tests mnemonic CRAP BF per p120 includes all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: CRAP BF: Cambridge low contrast gratings, Regan chart, Arden gratings, Pelli-Robson chart (m/c), Bailey-Lovie contrast chart, FACT chart. (Book p120)

questions.q: Pelli-Robson chart per p120 presents letters as ___ at an examination distance of ___.
questions.exp: Pelli-Robson chart (m/c): letters as triplets; distance of examination 1 m; contrast sensitivity affected before visual acuity (eg cataract). (Book p120)

questions.q: Match refractive powers per p121 (Gullstrand's concept) — 1) Cornea anterior surface 2) Cornea posterior surface 3) Lens … A) +48.8 D B) -5.88 D C) +19 D
questions.exp: Cornea anterior +48.8 D; cornea posterior -5.88 D; lens +19 D. (Book p121)

questions.q: Power at posterior surfaces of cornea and lens is negative per p121 because:
opts: Light is moving from rarer to denser medium
Light is moving from denser to rarer medium
questions.exp: Power at posterior surfaces of cornea and lens are in the negative as light is moving from denser to rarer medium. (Book p121)

questions.q: Match radii of curvature per p121 — 1) Cornea anterior 2) Cornea posterior 3) Lens anterior 4) Lens posterior … A) 7.7 mm B) 6.8 mm C) 10 mm D) -6 mm
questions.exp: Radii of curvature: cornea anterior 7.7 mm, cornea posterior 6.8 mm, lens anterior 10 mm, lens posterior -6 mm. (Book p121)

questions.q: Total powers in Listing's reduced eye per p121:
opts: Eye +43 D; cornea +58.6 D; lens +19 D
Eye +58.6 D; cornea +43 D; lens +19 D
Eye +58.6 D; cornea +19 D; lens +43 D
Eye +60 D; cornea +40 D; lens +20 D
questions.exp: Total power: eye +58.6 D; cornea +43 D; lens +19 D. (Book p121)

questions.q: Match Listing's reduced eye points per p121 — 1) P (principle point) 2) N (nodal point) 3) F2 (real image focal point) 4) F1 (virtual image focal point) … A) 1.35 mm B) 7.0 mm C) 24.13 mm D) -15.7 mm
questions.exp: P 1.35 mm; N 7.0 mm; F2 24.13 mm from reference; F1 -15.7 mm. (Book p121)

questions.q: Factors affecting refracting power per p121 include all EXCEPT:
opts: Difference in refractive index b/w 2 media
questions.exp: Factors: radius of curvature; difference in refractive index b/w 2 media; axial length of eye. (Book p121)

questions.q: Angle kappa per p121 is between ___; normally ≤5°.
questions.exp: Angle kappa (κ): b/w visual and pupillary axis; normally ≤5°; if ↑↑ or ↓↓ → appearance of deviated eyeball. (Book p121)

questions.q: Angle alpha per p121:
opts: B/w visual axis and anatomical axis
B/w optical axis and orbital axis
questions.exp: Angle alpha (α): b/w visual axis and anatomical axis. (Book p121)

units.title: Components of visual acuity; Snellen's chart and poor-vision flowchart
units.guide: Components of visual acuity/vision minimum visible minimum resolvable (tested clinically; MAR = 2 points subtending angle; <30-60 sec can't be viewed separately >30-60 sec can) minimum discriminable/hyperacuity (cannot be measured by clinical tests; eg stereopsis 3D vision vernier acuity) Tests for far vision 1 Snellen's chart minimum 7 rows variable letters per row each eye separately fraction 6 = distance of examination (m) 24 = respective minimum distance normal eye visualizes row Procedure 6m/20ft serial attempts if 6/60 not visible move closer 1 m increments record eg 3/60 at 3 m if not till 1 m finger counting FCCF+ hand movements HM+ light PL+ blind.
